# Role × Vertical Ranking

**104 role × vertical pairs across 26 verticals.** Generated by [`vertical_model.py`](vertical_model.py).

## Why the unit of analysis changed

[`model.py`](model.py) scored 179 roles in isolation. But **"e-commerce bookkeeper" beat
"bookkeeper" because of the vertical, not the role.** The standardised tool stack is what
made the work gradeable, the bench possible and the buyer reachable. So the unit is the
**pair**, and the top-weighted dimension is now `STACK`.

| Dim | Wt | Dimension | Anchors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `STACK` | **13** | Vertical tool-stack standardisation | 5=one stack every time (Shopify+A2X+QBO, Applied Epic, ServiceTitan)  3=2-3 competing systems  1=bespoke per client. THE unlock: standard stack = gradeable work = warm bench = free shortlist |
| `SAT` | **12** | Satisfiability | Objective output + client SOP exists + fast time-to-value + failure recoverable + not dependent on client's team. 5=binary right/wrong  1=judgment call |
| `RR` | **11** | Buyer remote-readiness | 5=already has offshore staff  3=growing  1=culturally resistant |
| `REACH` | **10** | Buyer reachability | 5=public named list (SEC ADV filings, state licence registries, BuiltWith/Storeleads)  3=targetable with effort  1=needs 1:1 outbound |
| `ICP` | **10** | Vertical size in the hiring band | 5=>150k firms  4=50-150k  3=20-50k  2=8-20k  1=<8k |
| `EOR` | **8** | EOR attach likelihood | Will they need us to employ the person? 5=no entity, no appetite, no choice |
| `SUP` | **8** | Offshore supply depth for this role+vertical | 5=thousands already doing this exact work for US clients  1=must create it |
| `AI` | **8** | AI durability, 5-year | 5=judgment/regulated/liability-bearing  1=being eaten now |
| `RET` | **8** | Retention | Async + no night shift + weak local counter-bid + no escape path + year-round |
| `FEE` | **6** | Salary band / fee size | 5=$40k+ placed  3=$20-28k  1=<$14k |
| `CD` | **4** | Competitive whitespace (inverse) | 5=nobody vertical-specific  0=a dominant incumbent owns it |
| `REP` | **2** | Seats per client | 5=hires teams  1=one and done |

**Gates** (⛔ regardless of score): `RET`≤1 — churns faster than it can be replaced · `AI`≤1 — role disappears inside 5 years · `SAT`≤1 — cannot promise a quality you cannot define · `RR`≤1 — buyer will not hire offshore

---

## The insight that reframes the search

The most acute US labour shortages are in roles that **cannot be offshored**:
dental hygienists (60–90 days to fill, ~90% of practices struggling, 11% capacity
reduction) [V] · ~110,000 HVAC technicians and a projected 550,000 plumber shortfall [V] ·
~82,000 truck drivers, with 92% of carriers running ten trucks or fewer [V] ·
530,000+ construction workers [V].

**89% of small-business owners hiring reported few or no qualified applicants; one third
had openings they could not fill** [V].

> You cannot offshore the hygienist. You *can* offshore the insurance verification and
> claims follow-up eating the front desk's day, which is how the practice gets capacity
> back. **Sell into verticals whose acute shortage is un-offshorable, by taking the
> offshorable load off the people they cannot replace.**

## Anchoring test

E-comm scores 5 on `STACK`, `RR` and `REACH` — **the three dimensions this analysis
derived from the e-comm case.** That is partly circular, so the ranking was re-run with
`STACK` and `REACH` halved (13→5, 10→5) and the weight moved to `ICP`, `FEE` and `CD`,
which favour bigger, richer, less-contested verticals.

| # | Vertical | Role | Reweighted | Base rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Marketing agency | Billing & project accounting | **76.6** | 17 |
| 2 | Freight/trucking | Safety & compliance documents | **76.6** | 3 |
| 3 | E-comm/DTC | Bookkeeper / accountant (A2X, close) | **76.4** | 1 |
| 4 | SaaS | Revenue accountant / rev-rec | **76.2** | 4 |
| 5 | Property mgmt | CAM reconciliation | **76.2** | 7 |
| 6 | Property mgmt | AP / AR / owner statements | **76.0** | 2 |
| 7 | E-comm/DTC | Inventory & COGS analyst | **75.4** | 5 |
| 8 | Staffing agency | Compliance & onboarding docs | **75.2** | 8 |
| 9 | Staffing agency | Back-office payroll & invoicing | **75.2** | 9 |
| 10 | Freight/trucking | Billing & settlements | **74.8** | 6 |
| 11 | Home services | Bookkeeping / job costing | **74.6** | 18 |
| 12 | E-comm/DTC | Supply chain / 3PL coordinator | **74.4** | 25 |

**E-comm bookkeeper falls from #1 to #3 under the reweight, but stays top-3, and the
same verticals dominate the band.** Read that as: e-comm's *lead* is partly an artefact of
how the criteria were derived; its *membership in the top tier* is not. Treat the top ~12
as a tied band, as with the role model (MASTER §7.10).

## CONSENSUS RANKING — all verticals including e-comm

defensible single ordering is the **average of both weightings**. A pair that ranks well

criteria derived from the e-comm case.
